sections.heading: C2 — Intersections and curves
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Intersections and curves

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A03
A jughandle makes a left turn by following a right-side curved lane back to a signalized crossing of the main road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A03
Traffic circulates counterclockwise through roundabouts and traffic circles, entering and leaving with right turns. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A03
Roundabout entries have yield signs and pavement yield lines. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A03
Most roundabouts have approach destination signs identifying the exit roads. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A03
Approach a roundabout slowly and prepare to yield to people in the crosswalk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A03
At the yield line, look left, yield to circulating traffic and enter only through an adequate gap. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A03
Inside a roundabout, continue counterclockwise toward the intended exit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A03
Use the right turn signal as the roundabout exit approaches. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A03
Yield to pedestrians when entering and leaving a roundabout. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A03
If an emergency vehicle approaches before entry, do not enter the roundabout and pull aside. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A03
If already circulating when an emergency vehicle approaches, leave the roundabout and pull aside rather than stopping inside. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A03
A bicyclist may use a roundabout as a vehicle or pedestrian; the vehicle role follows the same traffic rules. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A03
Do not overtake a bicyclist operating as a vehicle inside a roundabout. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A03
Pedestrians use crosswalks and splitter islands to cross the roundabout's legs. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A04
Entering a curve too fast can carry a vehicle straight ahead instead of along the bend. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A04
The greatest speed reductions are needed on sharp curves with wet or icy surfaces. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A04
Reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A04
Curve warnings are usually yellow diamonds, while a ninety-degree bend may have a large arrow on a yellow rectangle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A04
Chevron signs along sharp curves help show the direction of the bend, especially at night or in poor visibility. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A04
On a right curve, stay slightly right of lane center; on a left curve, stay centered. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A04
Reduce speed more as curve sharpness increases. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A04
Watch opposing traffic in a curve because a speeding driver may enter your lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A04
Look ahead along the curve's inside edge for steering guidance, checking each bend in a sequence as far ahead as visible. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]
